authoredPrompt: This figure is a single three-dimensional sketch of a vector broken into components. Three axes meet at a common origin, x pointing toward the lower left and out of the page, y running to the right, and z pointing straight up, each drawn as a thin line with an arrowhead and an italic label. A dashed rectangular box is built on the origin with its edges lying along the three axes. Three heavy blue arrows run outward along those axes and are labeled as the component vectors: A_x = A_x i-hat along the x-axis, A_y = A_y j-hat along the y-axis, and A_z = A_z k-hat along the z-axis, with each label written alongside its arrow. A single red arrow starts at the origin, cuts diagonally through the interior of the box, and ends at the far corner where the dashed faces meet; it is labeled A = A_x + A_y + A_z, every symbol carrying an overhead vector arrow. Drawing the blue arrows as three edges of the box and the red arrow as its body diagonal lets the reader watch the three components add head to tail to rebuild the whole vector. The same box supports the two nested right triangles from which the magnitude of a three-dimensional vector is obtained.
authoredInteractions:
- Preset vector cases: choose x-only, xy-plane, or full xyz components and the component arrows plus resultant update, showing when a vector is axis-aligned, planar, or genuinely spatial.
- Slider for component values A_x, A_y, and A_z: learner adjusts each component with separate controls; the box dimensions, blue edge arrows, and red resultant update together; the relationship between components and resultant magnitude or direction becomes visible.
- Toggle between simultaneous components and head-to-tail build: learner switches the construction mode; the blue arrows either sit on the box edges or animate sequentially from one arrowhead to the next before ending at the red vector tip; the equivalence between component decomposition and vector addition becomes clear.
authoredContext:
In three-dimensional space, vector A→ has three vector components: the x-component A→x=Axi^, which is the part of vector A→ along the x-axis; the y-component A→y=Ayj^, which is the part of A→ along the y-axis; and the z-component A→z=Azk^, which is the part of the vector along the z-axis. A vector in three-dimensional space is the vector sum of its three vector components (the figure):

This expression for the vector magnitude comes from applying the Pythagorean theorem twice. As seen in the figure, the diagonal in the xy-plane has length Ax2+Ay2 and its square adds to the square Az2 to give A2. Note that when the z-component is zero, the vector lies entirely in the xy-plane and its description is reduced to two dimensions.

A vector in three-dimensional space is the vector sum of its three vector components.

Vector A in the x y z coordinate system extends from the origin. Vector A equals the sum of vectors A sub x, A sub y and A sub z. Vector A sub x is the x component along the x axis and has length A sub x I hat. Vector A sub y is the y component along the y axis and has length A sub y j hat. Vector A sub z is the z component along the z axis and has length A sub x k hat. The components form the sides of a rectangular box with sides length A sub x, A sub y, and A sub z.

discrepancies: The red resultant vector A is strongly foreshortened by the default camera (which looks almost straight down the box's body diagonal), so the figure's main element appears as a tiny red nub near the origin instead of the long, dominant diagonal arrow spanning the box as in the source
The 'A = Ax + Ay + Az' label sits directly on top of the short red resultant and covers most of its visible shaft
The y axis projects down-right at ~25°, whereas in the source it runs nearly horizontally to the right — part of the same view-angle difference that shrinks the resultant
evaluation.notes: All primitives (axes, blue component arrows, red resultant, dashed component box) are correct with accurate labels, colors, and excellent interactions (component sliders, presets, head-to-tail build animation), but the default view looks nearly along the body diagonal so the red resultant — the centerpiece of the source figure — is barely visible and partly hidden behind its own label.
action_items: Change the default camera azimuth/polar so the body diagonal projects long and prominent (view more from the +y side with y nearly horizontal, as in the source) instead of looking down the (1,1,1) direction
Offset the 'A = Ax + Ay + Az' label to the side of the red shaft so it annotates the resultant rather than covering it
Make the red resultant arrow visibly thicker/more salient than the blue components to restore the visual hierarchy of the source
